docs.title: CipherStream Pro
docs.text:
CipherStream Pro is a hybrid cryptographic application that pairs a Java backend with a Streamlit frontend. It works at the byte level, so it can process simple sentences, emojis, and multi-language text.

Open the live demo

Educational project

A byte-shift cipher is not secure by modern standards. Do not use CipherStream Pro to protect sensitive data.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text:
• Generate a security key (vault.key) and download it.
  • Lock a message, including emojis and symbols, and download it as message.enc.
  • See a Digital Fingerprint and a Vault Health Check chart for your locked message.
  • Restore the original message with your key and your locked message file.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Use the app to lock and unlock your first message.
  • Get started to run the app on your computer.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: By the end of this guide, you will have CipherStream Pro running in your browser.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
You need:

  • Java JDK 8 or higher
  • Python 3.8 or higher

docs.title: Install and run
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository and open the folder:

    bash git clone https://github.com/sharmi-panda/CipherStream-J-Live.git cd CipherStream-J-Live

  2. Install the Python libraries:

    bash pip install -r requirements.txt

  3. Compile the Java engine:

    bash javac src/FileCipher.java

  4. Start the app:

    bash streamlit run app.py

  5. Open the address that Streamlit prints in the terminal, usually http://localhost:8501.

You should see the CipherStream Pro interface in your browser.

docs.title: Use the app
docs.text:
By the end of this guide, you will have locked a message, saved the two files that hold it, and restored the original message.

CipherStream Pro uses two files:

  • vault.key is your security key.
  • message.enc is your locked message.

You need both files to unlock a message.

Download your key before you close the tab

The key exists only in your current browser session. The app warns that it will vanish when you close the tab. Download vault.key as soon as you generate it.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text: Open the live demo, or run the app on your computer.

docs.title: Lock a message
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, under Key Management, click Generate New Security Key.

    The sidebar shows New Key Generated! and Key Active in Session.

  2. Click Download vault.key and save the file somewhere you can find it.

  3. Under Secure Messaging, click the message box and type your message. The box supports emojis and symbols.

  4. Click Lock Vault.

    Two results appear:

    • Digital Fingerprint shows your locked message as a row of hexadecimal values.
    • Vault Health Check shows a bar chart of how often each unique digital pattern appears in your locked message.

  5. Click Download message.enc and save the file.

docs.title: Unlock a message
docs.text:
1. Scroll down to Unlock an Existing Vault.

  2. Under Upload 'vault.key', click Upload and choose your key file.

  3. Under Upload 'message.enc', click Upload and choose your locked message file.

    The upload boxes accept .key and .txt files for the key, and .enc and .txt files for the message, up to 200 MB each. Your browser may add a number to a downloaded file name, such as vault (5).key. You can upload the file with that name.

  4. Click Restore Original Message.

    A green Vault Unlocked! message appears, and your original message is shown under Decrypted Content.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
The sidebar says "No key found. Generate one to start." You have not created a key in this session yet. Click Generate New Security Key.

You closed the tab before downloading vault.key. The key is lost, and you need it to unlock a message. Reopen the app, generate a new key, and lock your message again. Always download vault.key first.
